title: When I need to prepare for SOC 2 / ISO 27001 audits or respond to enterprise customer due-diligence
target_user: CTO, engineering lead, or de facto compliance owner at a B2B SaaS startup
job_to_be_done: When I need to prepare for SOC 2 / ISO 27001 audits or respond to enterprise customer due-diligence requests, I want to automatically collect evidence from cloud configurations, user-access reviews, and vendor certificates, so I can avoid audit delays, blocked deals, and weeks of senior engineering time.
painful_workflow: Collecting SOC 2 / ISO 27001 audit evidence by hand: screenshots of cloud and IAM configurations, quarterly user-access reviews assembled in spreadsheets, gathering vendor security certificates, tracking policy acknowledgments, and packaging all of it for auditors.
current_workaround: Manual screenshots stored in shared drives, spreadsheet-based access reviews, or paying for compliance automation platforms (e.g., Vanta, Drata) and compliance consultants; HN discussions frequently debate build-vs-buy and complain about platform pricing.
verified_facts: SIG-0001 describes manual SOC 2/ISO 27001 evidence collection (screenshots, spreadsheet access reviews, vendor certificate gathering) as a current practice.
SIG-0001 states companies pay for compliance automation platforms (Vanta, Drata) and compliance consultants.
SIG-0001 states HN discussions debate build-vs-buy and complain about platform pricing.
Stated frequency in SIG-0001: quarterly access reviews, annual audits, per-deal security reviews.
Cluster metadata confirms independent_sources = 1, source_type_count = 1, ecosystem = hacker-news.
inferences: Blocked enterprise deals (SIG-0001) imply revenue impact, but no deal values are given.
'Weeks of senior engineering time' implies meaningful labor cost, but hours and rates are unstated.
Pricing complaints on HN may indicate dissatisfaction with incumbents, which could be an opening — or commoditization and price pressure.
The existence of well-funded incumbents implies the category pain was historically severe, but says nothing about residual unserved pain.
assumptions: That HN build-vs-buy threads represent a broad buyer population rather than a vocal, cost-sensitive minority.
That a meaningful population still performs this workflow manually despite mature, heavily marketed automation platforms.
That the target persona would consider purchasing yet another compliance tool.
unknowns: Actual content, dates, and URLs of SRC-0001 and SRC-0002 — the primary evidence is not inspectable.
What fraction of B2B SaaS startups still do this manually vs. already use Vanta/Drata/competitors.
Any quantified cost: hours spent, dollars lost, deals blocked.
Whether pricing complaints correlate with switching willingness or merely grumbling while renewing.
Volume and frequency of per-deal security reviews for the target segment.
